author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: The relationship graph has a complete time dimension that no query can read: all 9,152 edges carry created_at and every graph subcommand answers only at HEAD

Every relationship edge in the tracker is timestamped, and no query surface can read the timestamp.

A census over all 2,301 tracked item files counts 9,152 authored dependency rows and 9,152 created_at values. Coverage is exactly 100 percent, with no gaps by kind and none by month across the full 2026-02-17 to 2026-08-03 span of the tracker. The data required to ask what the project graph looked like on any past day is already recorded, already in the store, already in plain text.

pm graph reads none of it. The command rejects --at, --as-of, and --since with unknown_option on every subcommand. All of ancestors, descendants, predecessors, successors, paths, impact, analyze, audit, communities, redundancy, dominators, slack, centrality, articulation, plan, and index answer exactly one question, which is what is true at HEAD.

The asymmetry is with the item layer, which already solved this problem. pm-hib1 shipped pm get --at taking a version or a timestamp and rendering reconstructed historical state without mutating, and it is closed. An agent can therefore ask what one item looked like in June and cannot ask what depended on that item in June.

What that costs is every historical question that is structural rather than per-item. Which milestone carried the deepest unfinished subtree when a given release was cut. What the critical path was before a decision landed, and whether that decision shortened it. Which items were graph isolates at the moment they were closed, which is the only moment the answer would have been actionable, rather than at HEAD where later backfill has hidden the fact. How long a blocker chain actually held, as distinct from whether it still exists. Each of these is a standard graph query over data the store already holds, and none of them is expressible.

It also bounds the recurrence and scale programmes. A recurrence model that folds historical defect families needs the edges as they stood at the incident, not as they stand after remediation. A relevance engine that scores a candidate on graph position needs the graph the agent would actually have seen. The distortion is not hypothetical and it is not small: 7,863 of the 9,152 edges, which is 86 percent, were created during 2026-07 alone, so a HEAD-only graph systematically overstates how connected this project was at every earlier point in its own history. Point-in-time projection is the one operation that removes that distortion.

Scope is a read projection, not a schema change. Edges already carry created_at, so the additive case needs no new field. Edge removals are already recorded in the same item history streams that pm-hib1 replays for the item layer, so an as-of edge set is derivable by the same reconstruction rather than a second store. What the work must settle is the disposition of the deletion case and whether an as-of traversal is served from replay, from a time-indexed projection of the durable graph index, or from both under a declared cost bound.

Bounding matters as much as correctness here. The graph surfaces are already bounded by default and pm-mfy1ux tracks the one that is not, so an as-of traversal must inherit the same row and token bounds rather than introducing an unbounded historical scan. On a million-item multi-decade corpus the cost of an as-of query is the design constraint, not an afterthought.

Every graph subcommand accepts a point-in-time selector using the same version-or-timestamp grammar pm get --at already accepts, and rejects it identically where a subcommand cannot support it; An as-of traversal returns the edge set whose created_at precedes the selector, with removed edges resolved by the stated disposition rather than silently retained; As-of results are bounded by the same row and token limits as the HEAD equivalents, and the cost receipt distinguishes replay cost from index cost; A paired test proves an as-of query at a past timestamp differs from the HEAD answer on this corpus, so the projection is demonstrably doing work rather than returning HEAD; The as-of projection is a public pm SDK primitive first and the CLI subcommand flag is a thin caller of it; Benchmarks cover a million-item multi-decade corpus and record the cost of an as-of traversal against the HEAD traversal it mirrors
Make the recorded relationship timeline reachable to graph algorithms, not only the HEAD snapshot
Historical structural questions become answerable from data already stored, and recurrence and relevance models can score against the graph as it stood rather than as later backfill left it
86 percent of all edges were authored in a single backfill month, so every HEAD-only structural claim about earlier project state is currently overstated and unfalsifiable

message: File point-in-time relationship graph gap: 100 percent edge timestamp coverage with zero temporal query surface
